result.note: Tests the July 2026 government position on ethanol-blended petrol: no return to E10, the mileage loss conceded and the forex savings cited.

questions.prompt: In July 2026, the Union government set out its position on ethanol-blended petrol. Consider the following statements:
items: It said E10 petrol could be restored for motorists concerned about mileage.
It conceded a mileage loss of 3% to 5% while citing USD 20.5 billion in foreign exchange savings.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the government ruled out ever restoring E10 or ethanol-free petrol. It accepted a 3% to 5% mileage loss but defended the policy by citing USD 20.5 billion in foreign exchange savings.
questions.source: Modi's government ruled out ever restoring E10 or ethanol-free petrol, conceding a 3% to 5% mileage loss while citing USD 20.5 billion in foreign exchange savings.
